name: Postmodern feminism
summary: Postmodern feminism applies poststructuralist ideas from Derrida and Foucault to feminism, holding that gender, and for Butler sex too, is produced by language, norms and power rather than given by nature. It rejects a single essential 'woman', a universal women's experience and any neutral view from nowhere, favouring situated knowledge, difference, and coalitions built on affinity rather than shared identity. Its explicit politics is thin, but it is generally left-leaning, anti-militarist and sceptical of both unitary programmes and state control.
scope: The profile represents the academic strand running from the French feminists (Cixous, Irigaray, Kristeva) through Judith Butler's Gender Trouble and Donna Haraway's cyborg writing, as summarized by Wikipedia and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Because the school is a theory of identity, language and knowledge rather than a political programme, most answers on economics, constitutions and foreign policy are inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist and anti-militarist writing and Butler's public positions, and carry low confidence. It excludes radical, liberal and Marxist feminisms.

keyFigures.name: Judith Butler
keyFigures.role: Philosopher whose Gender Trouble argues gender is performative and that sex is also constructed

keyFigures.name: Donna Haraway
keyFigures.role: Theorist of the cyborg and situated knowledges; argued for affinity rather than identity

keyFigures.name: Hélène Cixous
keyFigures.role: French feminist theorist associated with the school's psychoanalytic and linguistic strand

universal-healthcare.rationale: Haraway ties the erosion of the welfare state to the feminization of poverty, so a postmodern feminist would likely back public provision, though the school has no healthcare programme.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Haraway's account of the feminized, insecure homework economy implies support for better pay floors, but this is inferred, not stated.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist roots and critique of the informatics of domination make faith in markets unlikely; the school does not address market efficiency directly.

public-ownership.rationale: The school is wary of both privatization (Haraway) and centralized command-control structures, so adherents have no settled view on state ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Concern with the feminization of poverty suggests sympathy for redistribution, though no source gives a tax position.

unions-good.rationale: Haraway treats women's cross-race organizing around work as necessary, so unions are likely welcomed, but she also criticizes their unitary identities.

property-fundamental.rationale: The tradition treats rights and stable categories as historically produced, so an inviolable property right is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred only.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Haraway criticizes corporate high-tech and privatization as forms of domination, implying support for tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Haraway describes the dismantling of the welfare state as feeding the feminization of poverty, so cutting welfare runs against the school's analysis.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist-feminist heritage leans toward worker control, but postmodern feminists distrust totalizing blueprints, so no firm answer.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Haraway names surveillance and command-control technology as core instruments of the informatics of domination; Foucauldian suspicion of self-surveillance reinforces this.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Foucault-influenced scepticism about norm-enforcing institutions suggests leaning toward legalization, but sources never mention drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Butler questions the state's power to define hate speech and warns that censorship is complex, so adherents lean against statutory restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: Postmodern feminism rejects centralized authority and the single viewpoint, and treats power as diffuse; a leader bypassing deliberation is contrary to that.

state-harmful.rationale: Foucault sees power as dispersed rather than located in the state, so this statement is not their framing; mild disagreement.

limit-guns.rationale: No source speaks to guns; the school's critique of masculinized violence and norms suggests mild support.

empower-police-military.rationale: Haraway criticizes militarization and command-control as drivers of domination; Butler critiques policing, so more funding runs against the school.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources do not give a postmodern feminist position on sex work; anti-essentialism and distrust of fixed categories of victimhood suggest leaning toward decriminalization.

decide-locally.rationale: The school stresses situated knowledge but offers no view on the level of government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Foucault's critique of punishment as normalizing power suggests preference for rehabilitation, but this is an inference.

traditional-family.rationale: Haraway argues that the traditional nuclear family is being displaced and rejects organicist wholeness, and Butler treats kinship norms as constructed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Butler's critique of the heterosexual matrix supports equal recognition, though some queer theorists also doubt marriage itself, so not strong.

abortion-legal.rationale: Postmodern feminists stand with reproductive autonomy as part of feminism; no source states it, but it is the near-universal feminist position.

more-religion-public.rationale: The school treats grand narratives and norm-laden institutions with suspicion; no source addresses religion directly.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Haraway grounds coalition in the 'women of color' standpoint and attention to race; active redress is consistent with that.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The article states that gender is socially constructed and Butler goes further, holding that sex is constructed through language too.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Haraway rejects organic wholeness and natural origins as bases of identity, which undercuts nationalism, but nation is not discussed.

gradual-change.rationale: The tradition aims at destabilizing established categories, though Butler stresses subversion from within; not framed in pace terms.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Hybridity and boundary-crossing are central to Haraway's cyborg politics, so restriction is unlikely to be favoured.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Haraway fears global command-control systems while favouring broad coalitions; no clear position.

free-trade.rationale: Haraway links the global integrated circuit to women's exploitation in the homework economy, suggesting scepticism of free trade.

nation-first.rationale: The school rejects natural identities and favours affinity across borders, so national-interest-first is not its stance.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarism and Butler's nonviolence stance suggest wariness of military intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Cyborg politics celebrates blurred boundaries, but open borders are not stated; mild inference.

limit-growth.rationale: Haraway rejects organicist ecology and also technocratic domination; adherents have no shared view on growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Haraway criticizes the domination of nature and supports accountability in science and technology; climate policy is not discussed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Haraway embraces technology but warns it is also an informatics of domination, so she does not expect it to solve everything.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Haraway links high-tech militarism to domination; nuclear power itself is not covered.

revolution-justified.rationale: Butler favours nonviolence as an ethical position, but the tradition is also radical; the sources show no consensus.

experts-over-public.rationale: The school denies neutral expert knowledge: Haraway's situated knowledges mean no vantage point, expert or otherwise, is a view from nowhere.

central-planning.rationale: Haraway treats command-control hierarchy as a mode of domination and rejects totalizing theories, so central planning is disfavoured.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialist-feminist background fits worker ownership, but the school offers no stance on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: None of the sources connects postmodern feminism to land taxation, so adherents have no distinctive position and the answer is neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Concern with poverty and inequality suggests support; inferred only.

basic-income.rationale: Feminization of poverty and precarious work suggest support for unconditional income, but it is not discussed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist protectionism cuts against the school's anti-essentialist, boundary-crossing politics.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Haraway's suspicion of command-control makes state direction of strategic industry unattractive.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The sources say nothing about how property should be distributed; Haraway's socialist-feminist leanings do not translate into a stance on small ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Haraway discusses the homework economy but sets out no abolition of money or wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Market-fundamentalist proposals clash with the school's left orientation; not addressed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies imposing unity conflict with the anti-totalizing, affinity-based politics Haraway advocates.

one-party-rule.rationale: Postmodern feminism rejects a single correct viewpoint and grand narratives, so a party guided by the correct ideology is contrary to it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule rests on natural-order claims that the school's anti-essentialism rejects.

democracy-best.rationale: Butler defends assembly and democratic politics, though the school also critiques liberal democratic universalism.

direct-votes.rationale: No source on referendums; the school distrusts representation of fixed identities but is not committed to direct votes.

workers-councils.rationale: Socialist-feminist tradition is sympathetic, but the sources do not address this.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is not discussed by Haraway, Butler or the overviews; the school's doubt about natural national identities gives no clear direction.

natural-rulers.rationale: The school's anti-essentialism denies that traits are fixed by nature; the article describes its rejection of natural, fixed identities and the neutral perspective.

political-violence-never.rationale: Butler argues for nonviolence as an ethical position, but others in the tradition are not pacifist; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Haraway treats militarism as an instrument of domination and Butler argues for nonviolence.

separate-church-state.rationale: No source addresses it; the school's secular, anti-foundationalist stance suggests agreement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Appealing to a single authoritative text conflicts with the rejection of grand narratives and universal truths.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Haraway criticizes privatization and militarization; privately provided coercion is the opposite of her politics.

military-superiority.rationale: Haraway criticizes high-tech military buildup as part of the informatics of domination.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Haraway holds that unity should rest on affinity, not natural identity, and rejects organic origins, so a nation defined by ethnic descent is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Haraway says Marxist and socialist-feminist accounts still carry a Western humanist self and rejects a single master narrative of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Concern about material inequalities suggests support, but the school mainly addresses discourse and identity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Haraway's attention to oppositional positions of colonized peoples suggests sympathy; not explicitly stated.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial sympathies in Haraway's treatment of women of color; not stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Unity based on shared civilization is an identity-based claim the school distrusts.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Haraway stresses affinity, responsibility and partial connection, which clash with an ethic of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The school is sceptical of universal rights language, but it does not subordinate individuals to community duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Haraway rejects both the domination of nature and organicist appeals to natural wholeness; split.

limit-population.rationale: Coercive population policy would conflict with reproductive autonomy; not discussed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Haraway embraces technology and rejects a return to lost wholeness, though she criticizes industrial domination.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Haraway is enthusiastic about cyborg blurring of boundaries but insists on responsibility; mixed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Haraway's cyborg figure celebrates fusions of body and technology and 'pleasure in the confusion of boundaries'.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Haraway warns against command-control and coding the world as information.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Opposition to surveillance suggests support; encryption is not discussed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Haraway rejects appeals to a lost natural wholeness and organic origin.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The school holds that no knowledge is neutral, making a view-from-nowhere pragmatism questionable.

direct-action.rationale: Butler writes on assembly and protest as performative; adherents do not exclude parliaments.

means-match-ends.rationale: Frug and Butler stress that politics works through language and performance, which fits means that embody ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Haraway rejects organicist return to natural wholeness and embraces technology.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Haraway discusses the changing division of labor but proposes no abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not stated; the socialist-feminist background is sympathetic but the school avoids programmes.

production-for-use.rationale: Haraway analyzes women's work in the homework economy but does not state a position on production for need versus profit, so this stays neutral.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Haraway uses socialist-feminist labour analysis yet distances herself from totalizing Marxist theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Haraway criticizes Marxist unitary subjects and totalizing programmes; dictatorship of one class is contrary.

collective-farming.rationale: No source; programmatic collectivization conflicts with the anti-totalizing stance.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Haraway links militarism to high-tech capital but offers no inevitability thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: The school's left orientation and concern with welfare rejects the claim that taxes are theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Butler and Foucault question the neutrality of what counts as harm; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Butler's critique of fixed identity categories does not defend group rights, but she also questions liberal individualism; mild disagreement.

conscription.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarization suggests opposition.

exit-over-voice.rationale: No source; libertarian exit logic is foreign to the school.

state-as-business.rationale: Haraway opposes privatization of public life.

positive-liberty.rationale: Haraway's concern for material conditions of women's agency suggests agreement.

media-academia-power.rationale: The school sees power as diffuse, but academia matters; the statement's framing as exceeding elected officials is a critic's claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Anti-essentialism rejects biologically fixed categories; Haraway and Butler treat race and sex as constructed and read through power.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation by fixed communities presupposes stable identities that Butler questions.

total-state.rationale: Haraway rejects totalizing theories and command-control; a state directing every area is contrary.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rejection of organic wholeness and nationalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Haraway criticizes militarized domination and the school rejects natural national identity, so expansion by a strong nation runs against its politics.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by personal loyalty is a hierarchical form the school opposes; not discussed.

bound-labor.rationale: Haraway criticizes exploitation of feminized labor; serfdom is the opposite.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The article states that postmodern feminists reject the God's-eye view, and Haraway's situated knowledges hold that all knowledge comes from a specific position; Foucault links truth to power.

universal-morality.rationale: The school rejects universals and grand narratives; Butler argues that identity categories carry exclusionary norms.

single-common-good.rationale: The article describes rejection of one universal account of women's experience in favour of difference; Butler favours coalition over a single good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Butler is critical of some forms of Zionism, but the school has no stated position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; identity-based return claims conflict with anti-essentialism, but refugee rights are supported.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; nation-building identity politics is disfavoured.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist tradition suggests support for democratization of work.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Haraway's critique of welfare-state cuts suggests opposition to austerity.

economic-freedom.rationale: The liberal claim is not the school's; unaddressed.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moral example of rulers presupposes a unitary morality the school doubts.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial sympathy conflicts with scepticism of nation as natural identity.

force-without-un.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarization and Butler's nonviolence stance make unilateral use of force something adherents would resist.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The school critiques Enlightenment reason as a gendered universal, rejecting the claim that reason alone is the guide; but it does not endorse faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Haraway supports the welfare state and coalition across race; restricting to citizens conflicts.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Haraway's account of feminized poverty makes work tests unattractive; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Socialist-feminist roots favour conflict analysis but not as a master narrative.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The school deconstructs canons but does not call for destroying institutions; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: No source on blocs of states resisting Western powers; the school's anti-colonial sympathy is offset by distrust of unitary identities, so neutral.

workers-nation.rationale: Haraway rejects natural unity and national organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The article describes the school as anti-essentialist about gender; Butler argues no universal gender exists, so legally distinct roles are rejected.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest-bearing lending is never discussed by the school's sources; no inference is available beyond a mild distrust of moralized economic bans.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Haraway grounds politics in coalition of women of color and affinity; classifying people by race for segregation is opposed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Foucault's diffuse power view contradicts the state-as-tool model, while socialist feminists accept it; split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; critique of the domination of nature suggests disagreement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Haraway's valuing of hybrid and mixed identities opposes assimilation to one culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: The conspiracy claim conflicts with the school's analysis of power as diffuse.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are outside the sources; a coalition-friendly lean toward proportional systems is only a guess, so the answer is neutral.

national-mission.rationale: Haraway rejects the Western humanist self and colonial domination, so a nation spreading its own form of government is the hierarchy the school criticizes.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Postmodern feminists accept that women are subordinated, but Butler rejects a single universal patriarchy, so agreement is qualified.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist anti-elite claims are not part of the school's analysis, which treats power as diffuse rather than concentrated in a corrupt class.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Foucault's critique of biopower and normalization targets eugenic control, and the school rejects fixed natural categories.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Butler writes about state violence and precarious lives; accountability is consistent.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Haraway links the dismantling of the welfare state to the feminization of poverty, so confining government to defense and property protection is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hybridity, mixed and boundary-blurring identities are celebrated in Haraway.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Butler writes that some lives are treated as mattering less and calls for change, implying equality of worth, though she questions universal humanism.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The school offers no theory of socialist transition, so there is no basis for a position on socialism in one country.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Haraway and Butler criticize colonial domination in general, but the sources do not take up the settler-colonial framing, so this stays neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions are not addressed; the school pulls in two directions between equal treatment and respect for difference.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Policing identity boundaries is contrary to the school.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a subject in the sources; a ban on religious grounds sits poorly with the school's wariness of norm-enforcing law, but this is a weak inference.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular outlook.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Haraway criticizes command-control and militarized state power, so a state growing stronger under siege is the opposite of her politics.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Butler defends popular assembly but the school questions the liberal subject presupposed in consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export targets are outside the sources and carry no distinctive postmodern feminist content.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a group contradicts the school's anti-essentialism and coalition politics; Butler condemns persecution.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Butler favours nonviolence, but absolute property-based libertarian principle is foreign.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Haraway favours affinity, partial connection and responsibility.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Butler questions state power over speech while condemning neo-fascism; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Foucault and Butler analyze power as structuring subjects; domination analysis fits, but the neo-republican vocabulary is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not addressed by the sources; Foucault's view of diffuse power neither affirms nor rejects institutional checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Haraway rejects totalizing Marxist unity and a single revolutionary subject.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Haraway's attention to the feminization of poverty suggests adherents would put the poor first, though no source states it as a principle.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not covered by any source, so adherents have no distinctive view.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Haraway treats women's work organizing as essential to resisting precarity, so legal limits on strikes would be opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Haraway locates poverty in institutions and the world economy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Haraway celebrates difference, hybrids and partial connection, so the claim that diversity erodes social cohesion is rejected.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in the sources; its anti-hierarchical flavour appeals to the school, but nothing supports a firm answer.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Butler opposes state exceptionalism and writes on precarity.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price caps are not addressed; the answer is a mild inference from the school's concern with poverty and the welfare state.

party-controls-media.rationale: Haraway criticizes command-control of information, and Butler opposes censorship power.

party-commands-army.rationale: Haraway's critique of command-control and militarization makes party control of the armed forces something she would oppose.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship timelines are not covered; the school's boundary-crossing politics suggests a lean against long waiting periods, which is an inference.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for legislators is not discussed in any source, so the answer is neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The sources do not discuss supranational unions; the school fears both nationalism and global command-control, so adherents split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrating command of the armed forces and ministerial appointment in one office is the kind of centralized command-control Haraway criticizes.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by scholars of a sacred text conflicts with the school's rejection of authority claiming truth.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist doctrine the school never takes up; its anti-militarism is not enough to infer an answer.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Butler questions the state's power to define and suppress speech, and the school treats moral norms as constructed, so censorship for virtue is rejected.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term rules are not discussed; the school's wariness of concentrated authority gives only a weak lean against unlimited tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are not covered by the sources; participatory sympathies suggest mild support but nothing is stated.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; anti-militarism but no policy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not addressed in the sources and the proposal is a specific programme the school avoids.

people-in-arms.rationale: A militia in place of a professional army is not discussed; the school's anti-militarism pulls one way and its distrust of state armies another.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Organic and natural-wholeness claims are rejected by Haraway.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not discussed, and a nation as an organic unit is something the school doubts, so neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the school is largely academic.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anti-universalism suggests cultural relativism, but not stated.

death-penalty.rationale: Foucault's critique of punishment and Butler's concern for precarious lives suggest opposition.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The school treats gender as a construct and promotes its critical teaching; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Rejects religious claims but also treats science as situated; Haraway still defends accountable science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: MacKinnon-style restriction is a radical-feminist stance that Haraway criticizes for totalizing theory; postmodern feminists tend to oppose censorship.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based identity is the natural identity the school rejects.

minority-language-support.rationale: Haraway and Butler value difference and reinterpretation of language, so support for minority languages is consistent, but it is not stated.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law are not discussed; the school favours difference but doubts fixed group identities, so adherents split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Butler calls for troubling gender categories through performance and proliferating identities.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Haraway's account of global exploitation of poorer regions suggests sympathy for debt relief, though she never addresses debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Haraway ties domination to economic and technological systems, which supports this, but the specific claim about independence is not discussed.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not addressed; democratic sympathy suggests mild support.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Opposed to authoritarian development; Foucault's critique.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Haraway's global view of exploitation suggests a duty toward the poor, but aid as such is not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Haraway names high-tech militarization as part of the informatics of domination, so national nuclear forces are opposed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss constitutional design; adherents have no shared view on how heads of state are chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Insulating monetary policy from elected government sits badly with Haraway's critique of technocratic command-control, though she never mentions central banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims grounded in a historic homeland are identity-based claims the school distrusts; the issue itself is not covered.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: A socialist-feminist heritage fits a social view of property, but the school rejects a single common good, so adherents are split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Haraway criticizes Marxist unitary programmes but does not take a position on how to classify the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Haraway asks for responsibility and accountability in technoscience, which fits acting under uncertainty; she does not state the principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarization suggests wariness of mutual-defence pacts, though no source addresses alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Butler criticizes occupation in the Israeli-Palestinian case, but the general statement is not a postmodern-feminist theme.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The school is secular in outlook but wary of state power, and none of the sources discuss church-state relations.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional symbolism is outside the school's concerns.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Military force to hold a nation together contradicts Haraway's anti-militarism, though secession is not discussed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not a topic the sources take up; adherents have no shared position.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sacralized hereditary authority rests on the fixed, natural order that anti-essentialism rejects.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Concern with the feminization of poverty favours progressive taxation over flat rates, an inference rather than a stated view.

character-from-environment.rationale: The article says the school holds that identity and gender are produced by language, norms and power rather than nature; Butler's performativity makes character an effect of repeated acts.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Butler opposes exceptional sovereign power and emergency suspensions, so a ruler above law is rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Haraway writes on science fiction and technology but sets no goal of space expansion.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is outside the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass praise of a leader as the embodiment of the nation is the organic unity Haraway rejects.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law presumptions are not addressed; feminists divide on this.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Haraway criticizes Marxism's unitary subject but does not discuss post-revolutionary politics.

land-redistribution.rationale: Socialist-feminist roots suggest sympathy for redistribution, but land reform is not discussed.

refugee-return.rationale: Butler's concern for the dispossessed suggests support; the source does not state a general position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on shared nationality of people abroad rest on natural identity, which the school rejects.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Butler argues identities should be open to reinterpretation and troubled; punishing exit from a religion contradicts that.

women-must-cover.rationale: Butler opposes legally imposed gender norms, so a dress mandate for women is contrary.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed by any source; nothing distinctive follows from postmodern feminism.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity on ancestry is the natural identity that Haraway replaces with affinity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed; the school favours difference but also doubts fixed group identities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not discussed; coalition politics sits comfortably with equal rights where people live, but emigration to found a homeland is not addressed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The school gives language and discourse a constitutive role (Frug, Derrida, Butler), contradicting primarily material explanations.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is not discussed in the sources, so no position can be inferred beyond a weak dislike of concentrated power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Support for welfare protections makes strict no-bailout rules unlikely, but bank rescues are not discussed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Butler defends protections for minorities and precarious groups, which courts may secure; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Parity quotas rest on a category of women that Butler questions, but most adherents back equal representation in practice; contested.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A closed imperial economic bloc contradicts the school's boundary-crossing, anti-colonial stance.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Haraway's account of exploited women in the global homework economy suggests support for binding standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work motivation is outside the school's sources, so it stays neutral.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Butler's nonviolence and the school's rejection of vanguards make armed foco strategy contrary.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Natural hierarchy claims are rejected, so hereditary titles are unlikely to be defended; not discussed explicitly.

history-own-civilization.rationale: A centrepiece of national or civilizational history presupposes a unified identity; Haraway's situated knowledges favour many perspectives.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Haraway criticizes the Western humanist self and colonial domination; rule over a 'less advanced' society reproduces the hierarchy she critiques.

patriotic-education.rationale: Pride in a nation as an organic unit conflicts with anti-essentialism, though education policy is not discussed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Haraway's politics centres on women of color and coalition, so abolishing preferences is unlikely to be backed; not stated.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not part of the school's concerns and no source speaks to it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Haraway sees capitalism changing form into an informatics of domination but offers no prediction about collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence over former colonies reproduces domination that the school criticizes.

delink-world-market.rationale: Haraway describes global integration as a source of exploitation but calls for coalition across borders rather than withdrawal.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Haraway's global homework economy gives some support, but the thesis is not discussed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Butler's analysis of exclusion by norms and Haraway's coalition politics oppose permitted discrimination by private owners.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Butler's critique of juridical power and fixed identity categories cuts against entrenching rights, yet protections for the marginal are valued; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial sympathy suggests agreement; not a stated position.

elective-rulers.rationale: Butler defends democratic assembly, though she critiques the liberal subject behind elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Butler favours attention to those excluded by categories, but a veto for any single member is not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Butler writes on protest and assembly as resistance; the specific constitutional claim is not covered.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The balance of monarch and parliament is not a theme in the sources, so neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Haraway challenges the animal/human dualism and writes of kinship with animals; she treats the boundary as political, so animal suffering counts.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Haraway rejects dualisms and has ambivalent views on use, so adherents are split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist charity from the privileged is not how the school frames solidarity, which it places in affinity and accountability.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Haraway's cyborg politics is about responsible involvement, and Frug and Butler treat language and performance as sites of political struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Foucault's productive power through norms and Haraway's informatics of domination imply culture reproduces social order, though adherents stress resistance too.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Foucault's account of power operating through norms and institutions rather than force alone matches this claim of consent through culture.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Haraway describes a global integrated circuit that exploits women in poorer regions, which is close to but not the same as dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving office by birth ties rights to natural origin; Haraway rejects this.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations among communist parties are not discussed; the school's rejection of unitary programmes gives only a weak sympathy for autonomy.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not covered; Haraway's critique of exploitation does not settle whether aid or self-reliance is preferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist claims depend on organic national identity.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; sympathy to oppositional positions but anti-essentialism cautions against descent-based rule.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Butler calls the anti-gender movement neo-fascist, suggesting support for anti-fascism as a principle.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not discussed; the school critiques totalizing power of any kind but does not rank regimes.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The statement denies a settled historical point; Haraway's race-attentive coalition politics rejects it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; the school's attention to power in memory favours reinterpretation.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources do not address this; adherents may accept the need but object to framing it as symmetrical.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Feminist analysis of gendered power suggests disagreement with the symmetry claim, though not stated for this school.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Anti-universalism suggests acceptance that institutions are not universally suited, but this is not stated.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarization and Butler's concern with state violence make a political role for the armed forces something adherents reject.

paid-care-work.rationale: Haraway draws on socialist feminism's analysis of women's unpaid household and reproductive work and of the homework economy.

filial-duty.rationale: Obligation by family status is an organic relation the school distrusts, though not discussed.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examination-based recruitment is not addressed; neither the Foucauldian suspicion of credentialing nor merit appeals decide it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Investment screening is not discussed, so adherents have no shared view.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Butler treats family and kinship norms as constructed, so freedom to leave marriage is consistent.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are not covered by the sources; participatory sympathies are the only basis for a neutral lean.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatizing pensions is the dismantling of social provision Haraway links to the feminization of poverty.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure theory is not discussed by the sources, so no answer follows.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not covered, so this stays neutral.

single-official-language.rationale: The school treats language as a site of political contest and difference; enforcing one common language contradicts it.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; exclusion by nationality conflicts with boundary-crossing.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Foucault's view that power works through norms rather than intent supports judging by effects.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Haraway discusses technology and labor, not consumption; no source supports a view on consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarized domination and Butler's nonviolence stance imply opposition to funding insurgencies.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarized command-control and Butler's concern with state violence oppose a great power sending troops to keep an ally in line.

corporate-influence.rationale: Haraway criticizes corporate and military control and privatization as domination.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Butler's defence of assembly and civil society organisations suggests disagreement, though not stated.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Natalist policies treat women through reproductive roles; opposed by inference.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not discussed; boundary-crossing politics and housing concerns point in different directions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Concern for precarious, feminized work implies support.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the school is sceptical of exporting universals.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Butler defends civil disobedience, but the sources do not address a general duty.

non-intervention.rationale: The school objects to military intervention but not absolutely; not stated.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not covered by any source, so adherents have no distinctive view.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Haraway and Butler analyze power as structural rather than conspiratorial and reject blaming a group.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Butler's kinship critique supports separating benefits from marriage, though same-sex marriage activism complicates it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Opposition to secretive surveillance suggests support for transparency.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not discussed; Haraway rejects organicist return to natural wholeness but is not for global supply chains either.

informal-organisation.rationale: Haraway favours affinity-based coalitions over unitary identities and fixed organisations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Primacy of national over international law is not discussed; a mild cosmopolitan lean is the only basis for the answer.

religious-nation.rationale: A nation defined by shared religion is a natural-identity claim contrary to affinity politics.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is outside the sources; the school's redistributive sympathies suggest mild disagreement.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Possessions versus productive property is a socialist distinction the sources never discuss for this school.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; Cold War framing is contrary to socialist-feminist roots.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources do not discuss how public services are delivered, so no position is available.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist account is not the school's.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist critique stresses capitalism's domination.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Haraway presents socialist feminism's analysis of women's labour and the feminization of poverty, implying economic change matters.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialist feminists propose socializing housework, but the sources do not state whether postmodern feminists adopt this, so adherents are treated as split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Haraway and Butler treat language as impure, contested and open to reinterpretation, so purging borrowed words is opposed.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty rights of nations within states are not addressed; sympathy for indigenous claims is balanced by doubt of fixed group identities.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Haraway's affinity politics suggests small cooperative arrangements are acceptable, but the school avoids blueprint societies, so neutral.

majority-settlement.rationale: Engineered settlement of minority regions contradicts the school's anti-domination politics.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The school's anti-totalizing stance would reject both capitalism and orthodox communism, but no source frames a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Organic origins as claims are rejected, though the case is not discussed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Butler does not discuss denial but condemns political atrocities; holding it false history is not postmodern feminism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Butler's critique of the heterosexual matrix and of norms enforcing compulsory heterosexuality opposes criminalization.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Butler defends assembly and critiques state censorship; Foucault critiques repression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Butler opposes state power to define and punish offensive speech, so punishing blasphemy is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Haraway criticizes colonial domination and the Western humanist self.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamic legal doctrine that the sources on postmodern feminism never treat, so no answer is given.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Butler's nonviolence and the school's rejection of fixed authority.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Butler describes public assembly as performative politics, matching direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The article says the school attends to intersections of race, class and technology; Haraway frames cross-race and cross-gender coalition as necessary.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The SEP presents Butler as holding a trans woman's gender is as real as anyone's, and Butler urges feminists to support trans and genderqueer people.

assisted-dying.rationale: None of the sources deals with end-of-life law; Foucault's work on biopower cuts both ways, so neutral.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not discussed; Haraway is explicitly socialist.

alienated-labor.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist background carries Marxist labour analysis.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Essentialist claims about a civilization are what the school rejects.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority grounded in God is a foundational claim opposed to the school's anti-foundationalism.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not discussed; Butler's views on bans are not established.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Concern with women's subordination supports ending the legal silencing of harassment complaints.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mixed-economy models are not discussed by the sources; adherents lean left but distrust programmes, so neutral.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-militarism and nonviolence suggest sympathy but no school position.

rich-first.rationale: Haraway criticizes global hierarchies of exploitation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alignment between great powers is not addressed by the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Succession by descent assumes that rule is inherited naturally, a claim the school's anti-essentialism rejects.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit schemes are not discussed by the school's sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Haraway links welfare-state erosion to feminized poverty.

property-franchise.rationale: Limiting the vote by wealth builds in exactly the exclusions that Butler and Haraway criticize, so adherents reject it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Haraway says dualisms align women with nature to justify their domination, but she rejects organicist ecofeminism, so agreement on connection is qualified.

reification.rationale: The Marxist concept is not Haraway's vocabulary.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Haraway's critique of corporate control of communications supports it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Butler criticizes juridical power; liberal rule of law is not their theme.

racial-franchise.rationale: Haraway builds political identity on coalition across race, so voting limited to one racial group is firmly rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Haraway embraces technologically mediated politics, but warns of domination; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Opposition to secretive surveillance and command-control.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Butler opposes legal enforcement of kinship boundaries.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority is opposed by coalition politics.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Public deliberation is consistent with Butler's emphasis on assembly.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Frug's view that meaning can be reinterpreted suggests agreement, but it is not about religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Haraway criticizes corporate concentration of power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Butler's critique of heterosexual norms supports equal inclusion, though she is wary of militarism, so this is weak.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Butler's views on state authority oppose imposing worldviews.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Foucault's critique of prisons fits, but no direct source for abolition among postmodern feminists.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociationalism is not discussed; it fixes group identities, which the school doubts, but also protects minorities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Haraway ties the erosion of public provision to the feminization of poverty, so reliance on private charity is rejected.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed by the sources, so this stays neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not covered by the sources, so there is no distinctive position.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not stressed; the school focuses on present domination.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Butler's rejection of gender norms supports eligibility.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Butler's critique of gender roles supports shared authority; not stated in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are not discussed; concern with poverty and precarity suggests mild support.

abolish-ip.rationale: Haraway discusses information ownership critically; no clear view.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements are militarized, hierarchical organization of the kind Haraway criticizes.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Haraway's critique of high-tech militarism suggests support, though basing is not discussed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Basing of foreign forces is not discussed by the sources, so no position follows.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Butler on mourning and recognition suggests agreement.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Butler argues that sexed bodies cannot signify without gender and that the sex/gender distinction collapses, which the article calls the school's major departure from other feminisms.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Butler advises against defining 'woman' as the basis of feminist politics, and Haraway rejects an essential unity of women.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Butler's later work argues for an ethic of nonviolence but not as an absolute principle; the school has no rule against all lethal self-defence, so this is a mild inference.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Anti-essentialism and rejection of fixed, natural identities imply national identity is constructed and changing; inferred from the school's treatment of identity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Haraway's anti-militarist writing and suspicion of sacralised unitary identities suggest distaste for sacred veneration of national dead; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Haraway rejects dualisms and any good-versus-evil master narrative; politics is power, language and situated coalition, inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The school never addresses homelands; its stress on hybridity and affinity neither favours nor opposes a diaspora-centre model.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; the school has no theory of nation-building order.

god-not-male.rationale: French feminists such as Irigaray criticise male-centred language and its divine images, so mild agreement is likely, though religion is peripheral; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Its critique of male-centred knowledge and texts suggests sympathy with judging traditions by their treatment of women, though it rejects a single fixed 'woman'; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Haraway's coalition politics against the informatics of domination opposes group-based economic privilege; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Rejecting essential, unified groups implies borders need not follow a people; inferred from anti-essentialism.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist critique of the homework economy and of unitary organisations, which favours workers' own organisation over state-run bodies; no union position is stated.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist framing of the informatics of domination; she does not define socialism, so this is an extrapolation.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Haraway ties the erosion of the welfare state to the feminization of poverty, so public provision of basic services is inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: The school has no institutional-design programme; its suspicion of unitary power points both ways on a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Not addressed; Haraway's socialist-feminism criticises capital but offers no model of who should own productive property.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's coalitions built on affinity and Butler's coalitional feminism, which favour loose joint bodies without a single governing centre.

family-wage.rationale: Haraway describes the homework economy as displacing the family wage and criticises household norms centred on a male breadwinner; inferred, not stated as a wage proposal.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; Haraway is critical of biomedical power but also embraces technoscience, so the school has no clear lean.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; cyborg writing welcomes technological change of the body but the school takes no funding position.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; Haraway's critique of informatics-based domination suggests sympathy for privacy, balanced by no stance on payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's cyborg figure and Butler's performative, unfixed identity, which welcome identities not tied to a single legal self.

person-over-state.rationale: Butler's public work on nonviolence and the precariousness of life implies persons should not be sacrificed to collective ends, though the school also critiques the autonomous liberal subject.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Haraway ends the Manifesto preferring the cyborg to a goddess, rejecting both spiritual nostalgia and crude materialism; the school has no settled view.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; the school's thin politics gives no basis for a position on devolution.

gm-crops.rationale: Haraway welcomes biotechnology while criticising corporate control; no stated view on engineered crops.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the school; Haraway's writing on the informatics of domination gives no urban-density position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Anti-essentialism and Haraway's affinity politics reject organising on a presumed fixed group identity, racial included, though she supports coalitions of women of colour.

racial-pride.rationale: The school is anti-essentialist about identity but supports anti-racist politics; no stated view on pride in ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Haraway's anti-militarist writing on the military origins of cyborg technology and Butler's nonviolence imply opposition to wars of aims.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The school treats identities as produced by norms and power, not natural groupings, so language or history defining a natural nation is inferred to be rejected.

communal-electorates.rationale: Coalitions on affinity rather than fixed communal identity run against separate electorates by community; inferred from Haraway and Butler.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Haraway's writing criticises militarised nationalism and the school distrusts nationalist narratives, so a foreign-plot claim is inferred to be rejected.

free-public-college.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist writing backs public provision against the feminization of poverty; free public college is inferred from that.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Haraway criticises market-based informatics of domination; a pricing-first environmental policy is inferred to be disfavoured.

future-generations.rationale: No programme addresses it, but the school's left-leaning, anti-domination stance is inferred to accept a duty to those who come after.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The school rejects an essential 'woman' and any shared women's nature; Haraway rejects the natural unity of women, so distinct feminine values are denied.

arms-reduction.rationale: Haraway's cyborg writing attacks militarism and Butler advocates nonviolence, so arms reduction is inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The sources give no position on diplomatic secrecy; adherents' stance cannot be inferred beyond general scepticism of state power.

capital-controls.rationale: Haraway's informatics of domination critique targets global capital, so state limits on capital flows are inferred as acceptable.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed; the school is wary of state power but Butler and Haraway take no stance on arms control.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Haraway's writing condemns militarism and Butler's public positions favour nonviolence, so refusing orders to fight fits, though neither says it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Haraway ties the feminized, insecure homework economy to weak labour protection, which suggests support for collective bargaining; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Haraway's concern with the feminization of poverty implies support for top-ups to low-paid families; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Haraway links welfare-state erosion to women's poverty, so binding limits on public spending would be opposed; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Haraway's informatics of domination critique covers global divisions of labour, suggesting sympathy for rebalancing the world economy; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The school distrusts unitary programmes and state control but proposes no strategy of smashing or capturing the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Rejection of universal blueprints and a single programme fits letting communities experiment, though the school does not state it.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Haraway's critique of the commodification of everything under informatics of domination suggests opposition to pricing nature as capital; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The school rejects essentialist unities and foundational identities, so a sacred nation grounding lives would be refused.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the school's left-leaning stance on poverty and women's debt-driven insecurity.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the school treats power as diffuse and relational rather than regional.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Anti-essentialism is the school's core: Butler and Haraway reject a given human nature as a fixed ground of dignity, and Haraway's cyborg embraces redesign.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the school's left-leaning, anti-censorship stance, though Butler is also wary of state control.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The school rejects universal truths and grand narratives, so a single shared truth behind all religions would be doubted; inferred from that scepticism.

farm-price-support.rationale: The school gives no farm policy and Haraway's socialist-feminist outlook pulls both ways between state support and distrust of state control.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Haraway's writing criticises militarism and the military origins of technology, so an anti-militarist stance is inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: The school rejects a unitary class or women category as the basis of politics, so a single workers' party is not clearly endorsed or opposed; adherents are split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Adherents are split between opposing the practice as violence on women's bodies and the critique of universalist, Western framings of it; the sources do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal legal rights for women follow from feminist commitments even though the school doubts a single women's interest; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The school treats naming and categories as products of power, so respecting each community's own name is inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The school is silent on pollution law; it distrusts state control but also neutral legal categories.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses customary chiefs; the school is critical of power structures but also of universal models.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The school's politics is thin on environmental trade-offs; Haraway is ecologically minded but suspicious of programmes.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Foucault-influenced scepticism of disciplinary power and norms suggests opposing fixed punishments; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The school favours difference and distrusts norms imposed on groups, so a compulsory language rule is inferred to be opposed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The school has no labour programme; Haraway's socialist-feminist writing on work gives no clear view on closed shops, so adherents are split or indifferent.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the school's left-leaning, power-sceptical stance, which would see ID requirements as a norm that excludes marginal groups; it has no stated position.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of a single authoritative norm and its stress on difference; the school does not address state religion directly.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from its suspicion of formal neutrality and of any view from nowhere, which would find a purely procedural definition too thin; not addressed directly.

premarital-sex.rationale: Butler's critique of compulsory heterosexual norms and of regulating women's sexuality implies that sex outside marriage needs no justification.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its scepticism of state control and Haraway's cyborg politics of technology as a site of resistance; no stated position.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Haraway ties the erosion of the welfare state to the feminization of poverty, so replacing welfare programmes is likely opposed; the school has no income-support proposal.

women-suffrage.rationale: Though it questions the category 'woman', the school is a feminism and treats women's equal political rights as settled; Butler accepts the rights while criticising the category.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The school locates oppression in gendered norms and power generally rather than in religion in particular, and adherents differ on religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: The school treats identity categories as produced by language, norms and power, and Haraway's writing attacks natural racial and gender categories alike.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The school is sceptical of state control and of institutionalizing the category 'women', yet supports gender justice; adherents split and it takes no stated position.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist critique of the informatics of domination and of property relations.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its anti-militarism and Butler's public opposition to violence; the school has no stated position on courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of fixed truths and any view from nowhere; no source discusses scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from Butler's public support of gender equality and Haraway's critique of dualisms, balanced against its suspicion of universal prescriptions.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's anti-militarism and the school's scepticism of state control.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from Butler's emphasis on assembly and coalition, which favors direct participation.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from a left-leaning, secular school that rejects normative hierarchies; no source discusses national churches.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its stress on situated difference and rejection of universal norms.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from Butler's public support for self-determination and assembly; sources do not discuss plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's critique of imposed boundaries and dualisms; no source discusses colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's embrace of technology and rejection of nostalgic return to nature in the Cyborg Manifesto.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred as split: anti-colonial sympathies versus its suspicion of fixed identity categories and borders.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to gender equality and anti-militarism; a draft applying to both or neither fits.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Anti-essentialism and suspicion of unified identities make a fixed national spiritual bond unlikely to be endorsed; inferred, not stated.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Butler's public writing stresses nonviolence and the vulnerability of lives, so state killing without trial is inferred to be rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: The school has no foreign-alignment position; Haraway is anti-militarist but says nothing on China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from scepticism of nation-based identity and Haraway's affinity over identity; the school does not address kin states.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist critique of private appropriation; the school has no resource policy.

self-ownership.rationale: Haraway's cyborg and Butler's relational, interdependent subject dissolve the sovereign individual owner of the self, though Butler also defends bodily autonomy; low.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's concern with the feminization of poverty, which suggests relief for the poor from regressive taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Haraway ties the erosion of the welfare state to women's poverty, so universal provision is preferred to means-tested targeting; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Haraway's affinity politics and Butler's coalitions work through groups and assemblies and reject a single leader's authority; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning, anti-domination outlook and Haraway's critique of the informatics of domination.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Butler's public positions favour secular pluralism; inferred, not stated.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Haraway's cyborg writing embraces technology and rejects a return to origins and natural purity, so a return to ancestral values is opposed.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Women's autonomy over marriage fits the school's critique of patriarchal norms; Butler and Haraway oppose male control over women.

national-resource-control.rationale: The school has no view on national resource control; Haraway is sceptical of both state command and privatization.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Haraway's critique of the feminized homework economy implies that unequal outcomes can be unjust whatever their process; inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning, anti-neoliberal stance in Haraway's critique of global capital.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Butler and Haraway treat racism and its intersections with gender as ongoing structures of power, not as a past obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The school is sceptical of natural-law foundations, but Butler supports civil disobedience and resistance; adherents have no settled view.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist reading of the homework economy and informatics of domination suggests support for work reduction through technology; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: The school is anti-militarist and sceptical of unitary power but has no stated world-order position.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not addressed; Haraway uses Marxist-feminist analysis but the school as a whole is wary of unitary grand theories.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The school's anti-essentialism and suspicion of national identity make pairing patriotism with workers' politics unlikely; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Gender, language and identity are the school's core subject, so confining the left to material interests is rejected.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Haraway is sceptical of centralized command structures and unitary programmes, so a party-led model is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Sex, and not only gender, is socially constructed.
missingStatements.rationale: Butler argues that sexed bodies cannot signify without gender and that the sex/gender distinction collapses, which the article calls the school's major departure from other feminisms.

missingStatements.text: Feminist politics should not be founded on a single, fixed category of 'women'.
missingStatements.rationale: Butler advises against defining 'woman' as the basis of feminist politics, and Haraway rejects an essential unity of women.

missingStatements.text: Political solidarity should rest on shared goals and chosen affinity rather than on a shared identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Haraway's 'affinity, not identity' and Butler's coalitional politics put solidarity on political goals rather than shared nature.
missingStatements.declined: Largely a corollary of rejecting a fixed category of women (no-fixed-category-of-women); kept out to stay lean.

notes: Most political-programme answers are inferences from Haraway (socialist-feminist, anti-militarist) and Butler's public statements; the school has no party programme. Strands such as Butler's trans-inclusive feminism are contested by gender-critical and radical feminists.
